title: Gujarat Grants 15-Day Diwali Parole to 143 Prisoners From November 6
excerpt: The parole, a Diwali practice the state has followed since 2003, covers 103 men aged 60 or above and 40 women. Prisoners convicted of serious offences, and several other categories, are excluded.
body:
• Gujarat has sanctioned 15-day Diwali parole for 143 eligible prisoners, starting on Dhanteras, November 6, 2026.
  • The beneficiaries are 103 male prisoners aged 60 or above and 40 female prisoners, under a policy the state has followed every Diwali since 2003.
  • Prisoners involved in serious offences are not eligible; exclusions also cover those with appeals pending in the High Court, NDPS, TADA and POTA cases, and prisoners from other states or abroad.

The Gujarat government has sanctioned a 15-day Diwali parole for 143 eligible inmates across the state's jails, ANI reported on Sunday, describing the move as part of its prison reform and prisoner welfare programme. The parole runs for 15 days from Dhanteras, November 6, 2026.

Who gets parole

Under the guidance of Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, the parole covers 103 male prisoners aged 60 years or above and 40 female prisoners. Gujarat has granted 15 days of parole leave at Diwali every year since 2003, extending the benefit to eligible women prisoners and eligible men aged 60 or above.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2116814262933082162

Who is excluded

Director General of Police (Gujarat Prisons and Correctional Department) K.L.N. Rao stated that prisoners involved in serious offences are not eligible for Diwali parole. The exclusions listed in the announcement include prisoners whose appeals are pending before the High Court; prisoners from other states and NRI prisoners; those serving sentences under the NDPS Act, TADA and POTA; prisoners involved in terrorist activities or activities detrimental to the state's economy; those convicted in more than one offence; and prisoners involved in serious and anti-social crimes such as rape, kidnapping, robbery, dacoity, theft or extortion.

Parole is a temporary release, not a reduction of sentence: the 143 prisoners return to custody when the 15 days end. For the families involved, it means Diwali at home — the purpose the state has cited for the practice since 2003.
